descriptionChirho: To live, be alive, remain alive as an ongoing state of existence, including infinitive absolute emphatic usage (Qal stem); Arabic عَاشَ / يَحْيَا, Korean 살다/살리라, Swahili -ishi.
To recover, be restored to health after sickness (Qal stem); Arabic شَفِيَ 'to be healed', Korean 낫다, Swahili -pona 'to recover'.

labelChirho: Qal: revive, come back to life
descriptionChirho: To revive, come alive again from a state of death or near-death (Qal stem); Arabic حَيِيَ 'to come alive', Korean 살아나다, Swahili -fufuka.
To revive, restore to life, give life to someone, make alive (Piel causative-intensive); Arabic أَحْيَا / يُحْيِي, Korean 살리다, Swahili -huisha/-fufua.

labelChirho: Piel: let live, keep alive, spare
descriptionChirho: To let live, keep alive, spare from death, preserve life (Piel with permissive/preservative nuance); Arabic اسْتَحْيَا / أَبْقَى, Korean 살려두다, Swahili -acha hai.
To keep alive, preserve alive, save from death (Hifil causative); Arabic أَحْيَا / أَبْقَى, Korean 살리다, Swahili -huisha/-okoa.
Not the verb חיה; this is a prepositional phrase לָכֶן 'for yourselves' misattributed to this lemma.
